_note: Every fact the molecule lab states or uses points at a key here. Saved copies of each page are in .refs/lab/ (tools/lab_fetch_refs.py fetches them and writes .refs/lab/grep.log with the backing sentences). The pubchem-* entries are written by tools/lab_build.py; do not edit those by hand.

os-chem-7-3.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 7.3 Lewis Symbols and Structures.
os-chem-7-3.used_for: Valence electrons per element (Lewis symbols), the octet rule, hydrogen needing only two electrons, group 15 atoms forming three bonds and group 16 atoms forming two, single, double and triple bonds, hypervalent PCl5 and SF6 (why P may make 5 bonds and S 4 or 6), lone pairs.
os-chem-7-3.checked: 2026-10-01: page states the octet rule; 'hydrogen only needs two electrons'; group 15 atoms form three covalent bonds as in NH3; group 16 atoms form two covalent bonds; double bond in CH2O and C2H4; triple bond as in CO, HCN, HCCH; PCl5 phosphorus shares five pairs and SF6 sulfur shares six pairs.

os-chem-7-1.used_for: Ionic bonds as attraction between cations and anions; NaCl as a regular arrangement of Na+ and Cl- ions; Ca2+; iron forming Fe2+ and Fe3+.
os-chem-7-1.checked: 2026-10-01: page defines ionic bonds as electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged cations and anions; NaCl is a regular arrangement of equal numbers of Na+ and Cl- ions; Ca2+ is isoelectronic with Ar; iron forms Fe2+ and Fe3+.

os-chem-2-6.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 2.6 Molecular and Ionic Compounds.
os-chem-2-6.used_for: Metals lose electrons to form cations (group 1 1+, group 2 2+, iron 2+ or 3+); nonmetals gain electrons (group 17 1-, group 16 2-); ionic compounds are electrically neutral overall; metal plus nonmetal predicts ionic, nonmetals together predict molecular.
os-chem-2-6.checked: 2026-10-01: page states alkali metals form 1+ and alkaline earth metals 2+ cations; iron can form 2+ or 3+ ions; group 17 forms 1- and group 16 forms 2- anions; ionic compounds are electrically neutral overall; H2O2 and CHCl3 predicted molecular because all elements are nonmetals.

os-chem-2-4.used_for: Molecular formula subscripts; isomers (same formula, different structure), with acetic acid and methyl formate as the example pair.
os-chem-2-4.checked: 2026-10-01: page states subscripts give the number of atoms of each element, a subscript is used only when more than one atom is present, and acetic acid and methyl formate are structural isomers with formula C2H4O2.

os-chem-7-5.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 7.5 Strengths of Ionic and Covalent Bonds.
os-chem-7-5.used_for: Triple bonds are shorter than double bonds, which are shorter than single bonds (the lab draws them that way; the exact shortening factors are a drawing choice).
os-chem-7-5.checked: 2026-10-01: page states triple bonds are stronger and shorter than double bonds between the same two atoms, and double bonds stronger and shorter than single bonds.

os-chem-7-6.cite: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 7.6 Molecular Structure and Polarity (VSEPR theory).
os-chem-7-6.used_for: VSEPR: electron pairs around a central atom spread out to minimise repulsion; 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 regions give linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal bipyramidal, octahedral; a single, double or triple bond counts as one region; lone pairs take more space than bonds; the molecular structure names (bent, trigonal pyramidal, seesaw, T-shaped, square pyramidal, square planar); NH3 angles slightly less than 109.5 degrees; water 104.5 degrees.
os-chem-7-6.checked: 2026-10-01: page states each of these, including 'A single, double, or triple bond counts as one region of electron density', the H-N-H angles in NH3 are slightly smaller than 109.5 degrees because of the lone pair, and the water bond angle is 104.5 degrees.

cordero-2008.cite: Cordero B, Gomez V, Platero-Prats AE, Reves M, Echeverria J, Cremades E, Barragan F, Alvarez S. Covalent radii revisited. Dalton Transactions 2008, (21):2832-2838. Values read from the table in Wikipedia, Covalent radius.
cordero-2008.used_for: Atom sizes and bond lengths in the drawing: H 31, C 76 (sp3), N 71, O 66, Na 166, P 107, S 105, Cl 102, Ca 176, Fe 132 (low spin) picometres.
cordero-2008.checked: 2026-10-01: values read from the Cambridge Structural Database table on the saved page (.refs/lab/wiki-covalent-radius.html).

jmol-colors.cite: Jmol: an open-source Java viewer for chemical structures in 3D. Default element colours (CPK scheme as used by Jmol).
jmol-colors.used_for: Atom colours: H FFFFFF, C 909090, N 3050F8, O FF0D0D, Na AB5CF2, P FF8000, S FFFF30, Cl 1FF01F, Ca 3DFF00, Fe E06633. Colours are a convention, not a property of the atoms.
jmol-colors.checked: 2026-10-01: read from jmol_constants.js, the table the page draws (saved as .refs/lab/jmol-jmol_constants.js).

hill-system.cite: Hill EA. On a system of indexing chemical literature. J Am Chem Soc 1900, 22(8):478-494. Summary read in Wikipedia, Chemical formula (Hill system).
hill-system.used_for: Order of elements in the live formula when the molecule is not a named compound: carbon first, then hydrogen, then the rest alphabetically; with no carbon, all alphabetically.
hill-system.checked: 2026-10-01: page states the Hill system puts carbon first, hydrogen next, then others alphabetically, and when there is no carbon all elements including hydrogen are listed alphabetically.

ciaaw-2024.cite: IUPAC CIAAW, Abridged Standard Atomic Weights 2024, as stored in web/data/elements.json of this site.
ciaaw-2024.used_for: Molar mass of the molecule on the bench (sum of the abridged atomic weights).
ciaaw-2024.checked: 2026-10-01: weights read at run time from ../data/elements.json, which cites this source.
